claims.statement: Enoch’s §5.1 distinguishes conceptual irreducibility from metaphysical irreducibility and distinguishes identity, reduction, grounding, constitution and type/token claims. Mere supervenience is insufficient for his intended metaphysical claim.

arguments.name: Enoch’s indispensability strategy: introduction, partial book text and direct author reply
arguments.position: For justified belief in irreducible normative truth
premises: Normative truths and belief in them are instrumentally indispensable to that project.
bridge_principles: Indispensability to an appropriate non-optional project can justify ontological commitment; explanatory indispensability is a related instance.
arguments.conclusion: There is reason to believe irreducibly normative truths exist; a further moral bridge is needed.
source_locators: Google images pp.50–52/84; chapter4 and§5.1 limitations in A-P2T07-004/005
arguments.strongest_objection: Lenman's thin/thick dilemma challenges joint satisfaction of both premises.
arguments.strongest_reply: Enoch distinguishes merited standards, first-person warrant and value-sensitive instrumental indispensability.
unresolved_issues: Developed chapter3 pp.53–83, including epistemological defense, remain uninspected.
Chapter4 moral bridge and§5.1 now read; both are qualified and do not establish the missing derivation or premise truth.
Rejection of alternatives remains incomplete, explicitly at p.84 and§5.1.

arguments.name: Lenman's schmeliberation countercase
premises: Thin practical reflection uses scrutinized contingent concerns.
This activity admits success/error and deliberation-like phenomenology without robust truth.
arguments.conclusion: Robust truths have not been shown indispensable to unavoidable deliberation.
arguments.strongest_objection: Standards and similarity may not supply the deserved allegiance claimed necessary.
arguments.strongest_reply: Lenman regards stable concerns and critical reflection as sufficient without further ratification of the whole.
unresolved_issues: Sufficiency of the thin project disputed.
Not every Humean or epistemic-normativity response inspected.

arguments.name: Enoch's direct reply to schmeliberation
premises: Choosing versus picking is not proved exhaustive.
Formal standards may lack merited allegiance.
Replacement may preserve behavior while diminishing project value.
Justificatory evidence can vary without relativizing truth.
bridge_principles: A weaker replacement need not defeat the specified instrumental indispensability.
Phenomenology supplies claimed warrant, not truth-making.
arguments.conclusion: Lenman's alternative does not by itself remove Enoch's claimed reason to believe.
arguments.strongest_objection: Deserved allegiance may restate the disputed demand; private commitment needs a truth-directed epistemic bridge.
arguments.strongest_reply: Enoch invokes broader indispensability epistemology, permits premise error and distinguishes diminished projects from identical behavior.
unresolved_issues: Developed chapter3 vindication on pp.53–83 remains absent; opening and final p.84 are now read.

arguments.name: Enoch’s conditional moral bridge
arguments.position: For extending justified general normative realism to robust moral realism, given moral objectivity
premises: Assume chapter 2 has established moral objectivity.
Assume chapter3 has supplied justified robust general normative realism, after objections have been considered.
Common objections concern normativity generally; moral facts are proposed to be of the same relevant ontological kind.
The chapter 4 response argues for a non-wholly-contingent connection between morality and reasons, explicitly limited to a weak claim.
bridge_principles: A disjunctive treatment of moral and other normative facts needs a rationale once shared objections and the proposed categorical-reason concern lose their force.
This is a defeasible motivation challenge, not entailment from the two antecedent conclusions.
arguments.conclusion: On those assumptions, familiar alternatives to robust moral realism are under-motivated; other unconsidered motivations remain possible.
arguments.strongest_objection: Shared objections can impose continuing costs, moral and other normativity may differ in relevant respects, and the antecedent chapter3 case has not been fully checked. Naturalist or expressivist alternatives may have further motivations.
arguments.strongest_reply: Enoch contrasts accumulating costs with an objection defeated at the level of kind, and argues that moral objectivity requires normative privilege rather than mere etiquette. He expressly limits the result to a weak moral-reason link and an open-ended challenge.
unresolved_issues: Antecedent objectivity and indispensability arguments not certified by this chapter’s reading
No guarantee of a reason in every case or overriding moral priority
Possible further rationale for a mixed or naturalist view; §5.1 remains open to successful reduction

arguments.name: Enoch’s qualified resistance to naturalist reduction
arguments.position: Defeasible initial suspicion of reduction with openness to successful detailed proposals
premises: From the deliberative standpoint, Enoch finds purely natural descriptions insufficient without normative background commitments.
Conceptual differences alone do not settle property identities, and a naturalist can claim the proposed base is itself normative.
Familiar a priori/a posteriori objections and the response to Schroeder are not a conclusive general irreducibility proof.
bridge_principles: An initial intuition can bear defeasible weight without being unrevisable.
Specific reductions must be assessed by their details and theoretical virtues; inability to refute one is not itself metaphysical evidence for it.
arguments.conclusion: Enoch retains suspicion but allows a strong specific, including token-level, reduction to overturn the initial commitment.
arguments.strongest_objection: The initial normative-force intuition may encode the disputed non-naturalism; the naturalist may accept concept difference while denying metaphysical difference.
arguments.strongest_reply: Enoch acknowledges this impasse and treats it as a limit on the argument, not a victory; he asks for detailed reductions capable of earning their theoretical costs and explicitly permits revising his intuition.
unresolved_issues: No separately inspected Schroeder original or full naturalism critic/reply chain
No supplied successful token-level theory; no refutation of all reductions
How the incomplete chapter3 indispensability case survives a reduction that preserves deliberation remains contested
